summary.headline: Netweb Q4 FY26 revenue rose 86.6% YoY to INR7,737 million; FY26 revenue INR21,836 million (+90%), with a firm order book of ~INR2,100 crore plus INR327 crore L1.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR7,737 million (+86.6% YoY) and PAT was INR706 million (+65.7% YoY, 9% margin). Adjusted operating EBITDA was INR1,018 million (+71.8% YoY), with a 13.2% margin, while operating EBITDA after removing hedging gains was INR966 million (+63% YoY). AI systems grew 459.6% in FY26 to 43.4% of revenue, and management said HPC grew about 31% and Private Cloud was about 24% of mix. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 35-40% and operating EBITDA margin of 13-14%, with no major capex expansion planned; strategic AI orders are expected to execute over the next three quarters.

financial_highlights.metric: Operating EBITDA (Q4 FY26, excl. hedging gain add-back of INR52.4 million)

financial_highlights.value: INR833 million; company described as zero-net-debt

financial_highlights.change: Receivable days 114 (Dec 2025) to 86 (Mar 2026); inventory days 60 to 86

financial_highlights.value: INR3 per share (subject to shareholder approval)

segments.name: AI systems
segments.commentary: Grew 459.6% YoY in FY26 and contributed 43.4% of operating revenue, up from about 15% of mix previously. Management expects AI to settle around 35% of the business over time, with HPC and Private Cloud sharing the balance equally.

segments.name: HPC (supercomputing)
segments.commentary: Management cited about 31% growth and roughly 24% share of mix in FY26; it had historically been around 30% of the business. Demand is supported by the National Supercomputing Mission 2.0.

segments.name: Private Cloud / HCI (data centre)
segments.commentary: Share of revenue fell to about 24% from 30-35% historically because AI grew faster; management said it is growing at a good momentum. Pure server box sales are about 5% of business and not tracked.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance of 35-40% over the next couple of years, stated as enterprise-level and on an organic basis; management said the top-line guidance excludes strategic orders.
Operating EBITDA margin guidance of 13-14% for the next couple of years.
No significant capex expansion in FY27; only routine capex of roughly INR20-25 crore is expected.
Strategic AI orders expected to be executed quarter by quarter over the next three quarters; management declined to guide on execution timing precisely.
Cash conversion cycle expected to remain in the 90-110 day range, with inventory days likely to rise further in FY27.
Export share to stay around 5% of revenue while domestic demand is prioritised.
Dividend of INR3 per share recommended.
capex_capacity: New state-of-the-art manufacturing facility (15,000 sq ft) commissioned for new architectures and liquid-cooled systems; can scale beyond 150 kW per rack.
Management said capacity utilisation is about 65-70%; the company says it works on capability rather than capacity.
No capex expansion planned for FY27 as current capex supports the guided growth.
Inventory build-up of raw materials for large strategic orders and critical components.
demand_pricing: Order book of about INR2,100 crore plus L1 of INR327 crore (INR2,400 crore in total) entering FY27, which management said exceeds FY26 revenue.

Of the total, management broke it down as INR1,600 crore strategic, INR472 crore organic and INR327 crore L1 (per presentation). Analysts reconciled this as about INR1,600 crore strategic orders in backlog.
Pipeline of about INR4,400 crore; management said about 60% typically converts, over roughly 18-24 months.
Organic order cycle is about 10-20 weeks, with the organic order book expected to execute in 18-20 weeks.
Customer mix is about 50% government and 50% enterprise, with enterprise customers mostly large.
Management said it is not targeting hyperscalers at present; the market is seen as sovereign and enterprise-led.
Component prices are under pressure from AI demand; management said price increases can be passed to new customers.
Management said demand is shifting toward inference as well as training, and its product range covers both.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin not improve despite higher base business revenue, and are 13-14% EBITDA margins sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said strategic orders spilled into the next quarter rather than lagging. It said margins adjusted for forex were better than the prior quarter and remain within guidance; the 13-14% margin guidance was reiterated for the next couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the strategic orders be executed and what is the expected timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the strategic orders should be executed quarter by quarter over the next three quarters. It also said the company does not depend on strategic orders, with organic business growing on its own.

qa_highlights.question: Why has data centre business slowed and how big is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Private Cloud/HCI (the data centre business) was about 24% of mix versus 30-35% earlier because AI grew faster; it is still growing. Pure server box sales are about 5% and not tracked.

qa_highlights.question: Is the CCC target achievable and why did short-term borrowings rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cash conversion cycle was 84 days and the standard range is 90-110 days, with inventory days rising. Borrowings were short-term working capital for strategic orders, which the company described as transitory.

qa_highlights.question: Are the 35-40% growth guidance and FY27 segment mix inclusive of strategic orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the top-line guidance excludes strategic orders and reflects organic growth of about 35%. Segment-level guidance was not given beyond AI at about 35% of business and HPC and Private Cloud sharing the rest equally.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export outlook and promoter stake sale?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are expected to remain around 5% of revenue while domestic demand is prioritised. The promoter stake sale in February 2026 was described as liquidity-driven, with a 12-month lock-in on further dilution.

risks_watch: Strategic order execution timing: about INR1,600 crore of strategic backlog must convert over the next three quarters; management did not guide precisely.
Gross margin pressure from component cost increases and supply-chain constraints; inventory days rose to 86 in March 2026 from 60 in December 2025.
Working capital: cash conversion cycle of 84 days and short-term borrowings increased to fund strategic orders.
Pipeline conversion of about 60% of INR4,400 crore over 18-24 months, which the company described as dynamic.
Dependence on government and sovereign AI spending; the India AI Mission's pace of spend and the shift toward inference are open questions.
Hedging and MTM effects on payables affect reported EBITDA (INR52.4 million hedging gain added back in Q4).
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on demand and order book, but evasive on specifics: management declined to give segment-level FY27 guidance, component pricing, and strategic order timing beyond three quarters. Repeated answers on the large order book and government demand, with the margin and cash-cycle questions answered by reiterating previously stated ranges.
key_quotes: The defining highlight of financial year '26 has been the performance of our AI segment, which grew by 459.6% year-on-year.
The company is not dependent on strategic orders, as I have always been telling you that primarily the company is running primarily on its own organic way and it's growing in its organic way.
This is a technology company. This is not a capacity-driven company actually. We are a capability-driven company.
So the guidance on the top line is not inclusive of the strategic order. It is the normal organic order, which is about 35%.

adds.what: New state-of-the-art 15,000 sq ft manufacturing facility for new architectures and liquid-cooled systems (scalable beyond 150 kW per rack)

growth.why: Guides 35-40% revenue growth over the next couple of years (organic, excluding strategic orders) and 13-14% EBITDA margin, backed by an entering order book of about INR2,400 crore (INR2,100 crore plus INR327 crore L1) that management says exceeds FY26 revenue, though no capacity expansion is planned and utilisation is only 65-70%.
